human neural progenitor cells can be derived from human embryonic (hES) stem cells and that these progenitor cells can differentiate into the three neural cell types and migrate in the mouse brain.

human neural progenitors generated from human embryonic (ES) cells could be expanded in vitro and transplanted into newborn mouse brains where they migrated to different regions and differentiated into the three neural cell types.

human ES cells can be induced to differentiate into neural progenitors, that these neural progenitors can be expanded in culture and can differentiate in vitro and in vivo into the three neural cell types, that they can migrate in a region specific pattern in vivo, and that they can respond to local cues in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation and characterization of neural stem cells from human embryoid body cells and human embryonic stem cell lines.
the derivation of neural progenitors from embryonic stem (hES) cells.
the generation and differentiation of neural cells from human embryoid stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural progenitor cells can be obtained from human embryonic stems cells.

neural progenitor cells derived from human ES cells are a promising candidate for neural transplantation therapy, although further work is needed to improve the efficiency and safety of the transplantation procedure.
the human ES cell-derived neural progenitor cells have the potential to become a useful source of donor cells to replace lost or damaged brain cells in the treatment of neurological diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that it is possible to derive a neural progenitor from human ES cells that can be propagated and differentiated in vitro, and that when transplanted into newborn mouse brain, they can integrate into the developing host brain and differentiate into the three neural cell lineages.
the human neural progenitor cells derived from hES cells have the capacity to migrate, proliferate and differentiate in vitro and in vivo, and that they can be generated in large numbers.
we have shown that human embryonic stem cell (hESC) derived neural progenitors can differentiate into all three neural lineages in vitro and in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to generate a large quantity of neural progenitors that can be expanded and maintained in an undifferentiated proliferative state for a long time.
we have shown that neural progenitor cells can be made in vitro from human embryonic stems cells.

we have shown that human embryonic stem cell derived neural progenitors are capable of migrating along established migratory tracks in a region specific way, and differentiating in a region specific and appropriate manner, in the developing mouse brain.
